defects.title: ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS loads the plugin but silently drops its search_hooks(), so an env-var steer arm does not steer at all
defects.failure_scenario: main() resolves plugin names from --plugin OR $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS and calls load_plugins(names), but never writes names back onto args. cmd_mine then calls search_hooks_from(a.plugin), which on the env route is an empty list, so gp['hooks'] is never set.  Repro (both confirmed red in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP8/test_attack_wp8.py): write a plugin module exposing search_hooks() -> SearchHooks(accept=..., op_weight=...), export ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS=<mod>, then run `cli.main(['mine','--store',<cube>,'--label','close',...])` -> GPMiner is constructed with hooks=None (test_env_var_plugin_loses_its_search_hooks); with `--miner alphasage` -> BatchRewarder is constructed with accept=None (test_rl_branch_env_plugin_also_loses_accept). The control test with the SAME module passed as `--plugin <mod>` delivers hooks correctly.  Nothing fails: main() prints `plugins: <mod>`, the plugin's operators and its --fitness kind work, so the run looks like a steer arm and is in fact an unsteered run -- op_weight, accept, daily_fields, daily_leaf_prob and leaf_slots are all silently absent. This contradicts the design's "ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS is the env equivalent for sweep scripts" and cli.py's own --plugin help ("Also $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS, a comma list, used when --plugin is not given at all"), and WP11's Partura plugin is exactly a hooks plugin, so a sweep script that uses the env var will hit this.
defects.suggested_fix:
In cli.main(), write the resolved names back onto the namespace before dispatch so cmd_mine's search_hooks_from sees them:

    names = list(getattr(args, "plugin", []) or []) or \
        [x for x in os.environ.get("ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS", "").split(",") if x]
    if names:
        from .plugins import load_plugins
        print(f"plugins: {', '.join(load_plugins(names))}")
        if hasattr(args, "plugin"):
            args.plugin = names

(equivalently, have cmd_mine recompute the same --plugin/env fallback). Add a test to tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py: a plugin exposing search_hooks() reached through $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS must give the recorded GPMiner a non-None hooks -- the existing test_main_loads_plugins_from_env_var_when_no_plugin_flag_given only exercises `synth`, which never builds a miner.

defects.title: pipeline's GP-branch `warmup=trim` (design step 2) is not covered by any test -- removing it leaves the whole suite green
defects.failure_scenario: I copied the worktree to a scratch tree, deleted `warmup=trim` from the GPMiner(...) call, and ran the full suite: 905 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed -- identical to the unmutated baseline. The one test that drives a plugin scorer through the GP path (test_cli_mine_with_daily_fields_and_plugin_fitness_returns_0_and_records_contract_hash) only asserts `plugin_mod.CAPTURED` is non-empty; it never looks at the captured (dates, warmup) pair, even though the plugin fixture records it. Consequence: a plugin-registered scorer -- the Partura scorer WP11 will register -- would silently receive warmup=0, score the warm-up rows as if they were evaluation rows, and return a wrong fitness with nothing failing. The RL side of the same step IS pinned (test_run_mining_rl_branch_forwards_dates_and_warmup_to_make_scorer, confirmed red when I mutated warmup=trim -> warmup=0 there), so the two branches are asymmetrically covered.
defects.suggested_fix: In tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py::test_cli_mine_with_daily_fields_and_plugin_fitness_..., add `--warmup 3` to the argv (start is already dates[5], so trim == 3) and assert on the recorded pair, e.g. `dates, warmup = plugin_mod.CAPTURED[-1]; assert warmup == 3 and len(dates) == mine_store.n_days - 5 + 3` -- or just `assert warmup == 3`, mirroring the RL-side assertion that already pins it.

defects.title: test_cli_mine_defaults_have_no_daily_store_and_no_hooks does not test the "plain omission" its docstring claims
defects.failure_scenario: The recorder does `captured["hooks"] = kw.get("hooks")` and the test asserts `"hooks" in captured and captured["hooks"] is None`. `captured["hooks"]` is assigned unconditionally, so `"hooks" in captured` is trivially true, and `kw.get("hooks")` returns None both when the keyword is omitted and when it is spelled `hooks=None` -- so the docstring's claim ("not even hooks=None spelled out, just plain omission, which is what reproduces today's construction exactly") is unverified. Confirmed: mutating pipeline.py's GP branch to `..., warmup=trim, hooks=gp.pop("hooks", None), **gp)` leaves this test green (19 passed). The substantive assertion (no hooks leaked in) is real and the two spellings are behaviourally identical per WP7, so this is a coverage/docstring mismatch rather than a wrong behaviour.
defects.suggested_fix: Record membership instead of the value: `captured["has_hooks_kw"] = "hooks" in kw` alongside `captured["hooks"] = kw.get("hooks")`, then assert `captured["has_hooks_kw"] is False`. Or drop the "not even hooks=None spelled out" sentence from the docstring and keep the weaker claim the assertion actually makes.

defects.title: evaluate_factors' new daily_root was inserted mid-signature, breaking positional calls (no `*` marker on that function)
defects.failure_scenario: evaluate_factors has no keyword-only marker, so its 7th positional parameter used to be `label` and is now `daily_root`. A pre-WP8 positional call `evaluate_factors(store, exprs, start, end, symbols, max_symbols, Label('close', 1))` now passes the Label into daily_root and dies at store.py:131 with `TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not Label` (repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP8/test_attack_wp8.py::test_evaluate_factors_positional_label_still_works). run_factor_calculation is unaffected because it has `*` right after `store`. I grepped AlphaCube's src/ and scripts/ plus /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/{partura,scripts}: no caller passes evaluate_factors arguments positionally today, so this is a latent API break only -- but it is the kind a Partura-side helper would trip over silently later.
defects.suggested_fix: Either move `daily_root: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None` to the end of the keyword block (after `quiet`), matching how it was safe to insert it mid-signature in run_factor_calculation, or add a `*,` after `expressions` so every remaining parameter is keyword-only. Either change is source-compatible with every current caller.

result.notes:
Worktree /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering clean at bc3013c; base trees untouched (AlphaCube at 517fd09, Partura main workspace unmodified by me -- the pre-existing `M handoff/workflows/*/INDEX.json` entries are not mine). My scratch work is in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP8/ (gitignored): test_attack_wp8.py, test_attack_wp8b.py, and mut/ (a throwaway copy of the tree used for mutation testing). Run the attack files with `cd /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering && PYTHONPATH=.../src ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python -m pytest <file> -q -p no:cacheprovider`.

DESIGN CONFORMANCE (### WP8 steps 1-13): all 13 implemented, signatures as the design states. run_mining gains exactly one keyword (daily_root, after mirror_root) forwarded into open_cube_store; warmup=trim into GPMiner; dates=list(view.dates)+warmup=trim into the RL make_scorer; check_ban_key on the RL branch; accept= from cfg['hooks'] into BatchRewarder; the say() line; env.py's single `if (banned) or (hook rejects)` with its own counter/reason; daily_root on evaluate_factors and run_factor_calculation; --daily-fields/--plugin on the shared `common` parser (only research/calculate/mine inherit it -- synth does not, and all three thread it); --wall-seconds on mine; main()'s plugin block exactly as the design's snippet; --fitness choices= retired in favour of a scorer_kinds() check as the first statement of cmd_mine, with the long/long_hit + --cost-per-side guard left intact. meta.json's new "store_contract_hash" is design-mandated, not scope creep -- the design's own WP8 test list asks for "the run meta records the daily-aware contract_hash". Note the design is internally inconsistent about main(): the prose says names come "from args plus ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS" while its code snippet uses `or`; the implementation follows the snippet and pins it with a test, and it is precisely that `or` that makes defect D1 possible.

DEFAULT-PATH / RNG INVARIANCE (b): checked every new branch and all are inert by default. say() consumes no RNG (it only adds one stdout line); `gp.pop("warmup", None)` is a no-op since nothing sets gp_params['warmup']; warmup/dates reach make_scorer but neither PanelScorer/LongScorer/LongHitScorer reads them and GPMiner only builds a scorer when `_rich` (fitness_kind != 'ic' or penalty > 0), so the default GP path does not even construct one; the RL ban validation runs only for a non-empty tuple; `accept is None` short-circuits before any call and the `banned` boolean is truth-equivalent to the old expression, so one_layer_keys(e) is still computed only when a ban set exists; `gp['wall_seconds'] = 0.0` equals GPMiner's own default; main()'s plugin block runs only for non-empty names. meta.json gains one additive key and nothing in src/ or scripts/ reads a mining run's meta.json. Full suite reproduced at exactly the implementer's number.

NEW-PATH CORRECTNESS (c): RL and GP validate ban keys with the same check_ban_key and the same field set in the default case (generator.fields falls back to list(registry.fields) when `fields` is not passed; DF: keys go through registry.daily_fields in both), so --ban keys including 'O:cs_rank(DF:FloatCap)' behave identically on both branches. I verified dates/warmup line up with the panel the scorer is handed: len(dates) == target rows on the RL path (attack test D in test_attack_wp8b.py) and GPMiner passes the same full self.view.dates, so a plugin scorer sees a consistent (full axis, warmup offset) pair on both branches. All four RL miners funnel through BatchRewarder.rewards, so the accept hook has a single choke point; TokenEnv never evaluates. available(store.daily) and resolve(store=None) make cli.py's "--daily-fields ... the three derived fields resolve even with no directory at all" help text accurate. Both store classes carry .daily and .contract_hash, so the say() line and the meta key work for segmented stores too.

TEST QUALITY (d): 6 of 8 targeted mutations are caught by the new file -- dropping daily_root from open_cube_store, RL warmup=trim -> 0, dropping the accept= forward, deleting the RL check_ban_key loop, deleting cmd_mine's scorer_kinds check, and collapsing the accept refusal into the banned counter/reason (which also pins that a banned candidate short-circuits before the hook and that the engine is never called). Deleting the say() else-branch is caught too. The two misses are defects D3 and D4 above. The test_production.py edit is real: cmd_mine is imported inside that test, and removing the scorer_kinds check makes it fail with FileNotFoundError instead of SystemExit (mutation-verified).

FILES OUTSIDE THE OWNED LIST (e): only tests/test_production.py, declared by the implementer, one assertion, minimal and correct. Also worth knowing: test_production.py::test_cli_mine_accepts_every_run_mining_knob greps cmd_mine's source for `a.<name>` and asserts each exists on the namespace, so it already guards --plugin/--daily-fields/--wall-seconds against a missing parser argument.

THE TWO DECLARED DEVIATIONS -- both check out. (1) export_run_to_parquet left un-threaded: verified safe, it only reads store.view()/read_status() for lifecycle masking and never evaluates a leaf. `calculate --daily-fields --expr cap=FloatCap --parquet` runs end to end and writes parquet (attack A), and so does the same run with ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS exported instead (attack B), where export's own open_cube_store picks the env var up and require_board_rule passes. (2) `gp.pop("warmup", None)`: correct and needed, since nothing sets gp_params['warmup'] today but doing so would otherwise be a duplicate-keyword TypeError -- the only cost is that it drops such a value silently rather than erroring.

TWO MORE THINGS, NOT DEFECTS. (i) cmd_research threads daily_root into open_cube_store rather than into evaluate_factors, so evaluate_factors' own new keyword is dead on the CLI path -- equivalent for a bare-minute store, and the library-level test covers the keyword directly. Separately, `research --store <compute_root>` crashes at research.py:109 with `TypeError: ... not SegmentedCubeStore` BOTH with and without --daily-fields (attack C and its control): pre-existing, and the design explicitly told WP8 to leave that open_cube_store inconsistency alone. (ii) BatchRewarder(accept=...) does no eager validation, unlike TypedTreeGenerator's _check_accept_hook, so a malformed RL-side hook fails mid-run with a TypeError instead of at construction -- a small parity gap the design did not ask for. One observation for whoever owns WP5/WP11: a plugin whose hooks set daily_fields=('FloatCap',) with no --daily-fields given runs to completion with rc 0 and no daily leaf in the pool (attack test in test_attack_wp8.py) -- the new say() line ("daily fields: none attached") is the only signal, which is what the design intended, but it means a misconfigured sweep arm burns its whole budget quietly.
